author: NorthEast News Desk
body: HDFC Bank’s board has submitted two candidates to the Reserve Bank of India for approval as the private lender’s next chief executive, Reuters reported. The candidates were not named. The selection will determine the successor to Sashidhar Jagdishan, who is scheduled to retire when his second term ends in October.

Indian private banks must obtain the central bank’s prior approval before appointing a chief executive, giving the regulator a direct role in the succession. HDFC Bank has also reappointed V. Srinivasa Rangan as a whole-time director and named Jimmy Tata to the same type of position. The incoming CEO is expected to fill a fourth whole-time director role.

Leadership continuity matters for HDFC Bank because of its scale and the operational demands of its expanded franchise. The board’s submission moves the process into the regulatory phase but does not indicate which candidate is preferred or when the RBI will decide. Investors will be watching for the nominee’s priorities on growth, asset quality and integration. Until approval is announced, the bank’s existing leadership remains responsible for managing the transition toward Jagdishan’s October departure.
dek: The unnamed nominees require Reserve Bank of India approval before Sashidhar Jagdishan’s second term ends in October.
headline: HDFC Bank submits two CEO candidates to India’s central bank
